channel.title: JustinCredible Space
channel.description: Rockets, launches, satellites and missions beyond Earth.

item.title: Update: Starship Flight 15's Booster Catch Was Aborted, and SpaceX Plans Its First-Ever Ship Catch Saturday Afternoon
item.description: SpaceX's Super Heavy booster aborted its tower catch on Friday, November 13, 2026, after detecting a guidance issue and splashed down in the Gulf. The Ship upper stage is in orbit, and SpaceX plans to try catching it at Starbase around 3:20 p.m. Central on Saturday.

item.title: Update: Starship Flight 15 Targets Friday Launch and Double Catch, but the FAA License Was Still Pending Friday Morning
item.description: SpaceX is targeting 4:45 p.m. CT on November 13, 2026, for Starship Flight 15, its first attempt to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the Starship upper stage. As of Friday morning the FAA had not issued the launch license.

item.title: SpaceX Picks Qualcomm to Power Starlink Mobile's 5G Cell Sites
item.description: Qualcomm will supply Dragonwing radio and baseband platforms for tens of thousands of Starlink Mobile cell sites in the US, with the rollout starting in 2027. Financial terms weren't disclosed.

item.title: SpaceX Is Reportedly in Talks to Buy Boost Mobile
item.description: The Washington Post reports SpaceX has been talking with EchoStar about buying Boost Mobile or getting access to its network, a possible shortcut into the US wireless market for Starlink Mobile. No deal has been announced.

item.title: Google's AI Satellite Wrote Its First Haiku From Orbit
item.description: Google's Project Suncatcher prototype ran its Gemma 4 model on a data-center-class TPU in space and sent back a poem. It's an early test of whether AI computing could one day move off the planet.

item.title: SpaceX Will Try to Catch the WHOLE Starship on Flight 15
item.description: On its Oct 20 earnings call, SpaceX said Starship Flight 15 (targeting November) will try to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the Starship upper stage with the tower's chopsticks. FAA license still pending.

item.title: Sunday Rocket Matinee: Falcon 9 Hauls Three SES O3b mPOWER Sats
item.description: SpaceX is targeting Sunday Sep 13 for a Falcon 9 launch of three SES O3b mPOWER satellites from Cape Canaveral — the first triple mPOWER stack — window open 2:49 p.m. ET. A consumer guide to the afternoon broadband rocket.

item.title: Starship Flight 14 Is One Week Out — On the FAA Calendar, Anyway
item.description: Airspace advisories still point to Friday Sep 18 (~12:15–14:14 UTC) with Sep 19 backup for Starship Flight 14 — while SpaceX hasn’t locked a public webcast or date. Here’s the countdown-week checklist, not another mission remake.

item.title: Starship Flight 14: First Real Orbit + Starlink V3 That Actually Stays Up
item.description: SpaceX’s FCC paperwork points to a mid-September window for Starship Flight 14—the program’s first full orbital profile and the first shot at parking Starlink V3 sats in a staying orbit.

item.title: NASA and IBM just open-sourced a foundation model for the Moon
item.description: On September 10, 2026, NASA and IBM released a lunar AI foundation model on Hugging Face — craters, volcanic quirks, polar ice, and why that ice matters.

item.title: Starlink at home and in your pocket: what’s real in 2026
item.description: Dish broadband and Direct-to-Cell are both real — but they’re not one magical plan yet. Here’s the clear, accurate split for home internet vs phone satellite.
